messages:
sachin: heads-up, I found a weird perf regression in the KV layout path when running paged-attention on interleaved KV with uint8 quantization. numbers below, reproducible on a8g. :thinking:

sachin: micro-bench (single request, seq=2048, bs=1, kv_len=8192)
- fused_attn + separate-kv + fp16: 3.6 ms/token
- paged_attn + separate-kv + fp16: 3.8 ms/token
- paged_attn + interleaved-kv + fp16: 4.2 ms/token  <-- expected ~3.9
- paged_attn + interleaved-kv + uint8: 6.5 ms/token  <-- big slow-down

sachin: stack looks like extra memcpy / uncoalesced loads in the quant path. nvprof shows a lot of L2 stalls and some memcopies showing up in the host->device side for the uint8 case.

maria: can you paste the exact recreate command? I want to run on my perf box.

sachin: sure — this is the repro I used:
```
./run_bench --attn=paged --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=uint8 --seq=2048 --kv_len=8192 --bs=1 --profile=cupti
```
I added --pad-kv=128 and got a 10% win for uint8, so alignment matters.

alex: interesting. the kernel selector currently prefers paged for long KV but we added a fast-path assuming 128b alignment for vector loads. if interleaved layout results in stride != 128 then mem access falls back and kills perf.

ellie: can you dump the actual stride bytes and alignment from the allocator? we might be miscomputing pitch for quantized tensors. also: what about dtype promotion in the attention kernel? uint8->int8->int32 accumulation could be hitting a fallback.

sachin: allocator dump: base_ptr 0x7fab34000000 (aligned 64b), kv_stride=320 bytes per token (interleaved), kv_stride % 128 = 64 -> misaligned for our 128b vector load.

maria: aha. two options: (1) pad every allocation to 128b boundary (more memory), (2) change kernel to handle 64b stride with masked loads but that regresses fused path. For perf eval I'd try (1) as a quick guard.

alex: kernel-selection fix: we should detect runtime-alignment and prefer fused-attn or separate-kv when vector-width assumptions don't hold. currently the heuristic only checks seq/kv length and hw capability, not stride alignment. :eyes:

perf-bot: perf-summary attached: 1778454321_paged-interleave-uint8.log -> mean 6.47 ms/token, p95 9.2 ms/token. baseline fused/fp16 p95 4.1 ms/token.

ellie: small experiment idea: keep interleaved layout but align per-row to 256 bytes (power-of-two), that should satisfy all vector widths (128/256). try to change the allocator to round up row stride to 256 and rebench.

maria: I pushed a branch (kv/align-pad-256) that changes the per-row stride rounding and adds a flag --kv-min-align. quick summary: on a8g, uint8 case went from 6.5 -> 4.3 ms/token with pad=256. memory overhead ~ +6% for kv buffers.

sachin: great. can we avoid forcing 256 for small models? maybe runtime chooses paddings only when the selected attention kernel needs it. we can add a small check in kernel selector: if layout==interleaved and dtype in (uint8,int8) and stride%128!=0 then prefer fused or enable padding.

alex: agreed. I'll sketch a heuristic: if padding overhead > 10% memory and bs>8 then prefer fused-attn, else pad. also track fallback counters to surface in console.

ellie: also worth noting that paging interacts: small page sizes amplify misalignment because page chunking doesn't respect high-level row rounding. we should fold page boundaries into allocator rounding so mapped fragments remain aligned.

maria: added unit tests that simulate misaligned stride and assert selector picks fallback or pads. ran internal perf CI — preliminary green.

sachin: i'll open a tracking PR with perf numbers + recommended selector patch + allocator option. jira INF-2147 for the regression. assign to alex for selector, ellie for allocator.

alex: will take selector. quick win: expose --kv-min-align and default to 256 for quant path. then we can iterate.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) validate memory overhead on Dedicated configs, (2) add trace events for padding decisions, (3) add perf alert when p95 regresses >20% for attention routes.

sachin: leaving logs and nvprof traces in s3://redwood-perf/1778454321/. ping if you need access. :+1:

ellie: nice catch. documented in the thread and will update eng-runtime runbook for KV alignment gotchas.

perf-bot: benchmark job finished: 1778454321 -> success. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1778454321/{profile,bench-summary}.json

maria: I'll link the PR here when open. closing loop soon. :rocket:
